prs.author: sebastian-velten
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth token endpoints on some servers return URL-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) responses instead of JSON, causing the client to fail when parsing the token response. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth token endpoints on some servers return URL-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) responses instead of JSON, causing the client to fail when parsing the token response. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #1511 addresses the root cause directly by adding content-type detection and URL-encoded response parsing in `_handle_token_response`, making the client resilient regardless of what format the server returns. PR #1531 only adds `Accept: application/json` request headers, which is a best-effort hint that non-compliant servers may ignore — it does not fix parsing if a server still returns form-encoded data. #1511's approach is a superset: it handles the problem even when the Accept header is not honored. The two fixes should be combined (the Accept header from #1531 is a worthwhile addition), but #1511 contains the substantive fix and should be the base.
